name: Jonker Street and Chinatown
tagline: The Peranakan heart, shophouses and the weekend night market
description: The historic Chinese quarter west of the river, built along Jonker Street with two-storey shophouses, clan associations, antique shops and the Baba Nyonya heritage museum. On Friday and Saturday evenings the street closes for a night market that fills the whole quarter.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the Peranakan quarter and the night market at the door
pros: Jonker Street's shops, museums and night market
The best Nyonya restaurants in the city
Everything in the historic core walkable
cons: Shophouse rooms are small and can be dark
Tourist pricing on the main street

name: Dutch Square and the Riverside
tagline: The red Stadthuys and the walk along the water
description: The colonial core east of the river around the terracotta Stadthuys, Christ Church and the climb to St Paul's ruins on the hill, with the cleaned-up river walk running below. It is the postcard quarter and the museums are concentrated here, with the river cruise leaving from the quay.
bestFor: Stays that want the museums and the riverside at the door
pros: The Stadthuys, St Paul's and the museums together
River walk and cruise from the quay
Central for everything in the old town
cons: The trishaws are loud and constant

name: Bukit Baru and Ayer Keroh
tagline: The modern suburbs east, where residents live
description: The residential districts spreading east and northeast from the old town, with modern apartment blocks and terraced housing, supermarkets, schools and the Melaka campus of several universities. Rents here are a fraction of the historic core and it is the practical choice for a longer stay.
bestFor: Longer stays where the old town rents are unnecessary
pros: Rents well below the historic core
Modern flats with parking and facilities
cons: Twenty minutes from the old town
Requires a car or Grab for everything

name: Klebang and the Coast
tagline: The reclaimed shoreline west, with the beach and the sunsets
description: The coastal strip northwest of the centre along reclaimed land, with Klebang beach, the coconut shake stalls that are a genuine local institution, and newer waterfront apartment developments. The sunsets over the Straits are the draw and the sea itself is not for swimming.
bestFor: Stays wanting a sea view and newer apartments
pros: Sunset views over the Straits of Malacca
cons: Fifteen minutes from the historic core

name: Portuguese Settlement
tagline: The Kristang community east of the centre
description: A small coastal district settled by the descendants of Portuguese who arrived in 1511, who speak Kristang, a Portuguese-based creole, and maintain their own festivals and cuisine. The seafood restaurants along the waterfront are the main draw and the community is a genuine cultural survival.
bestFor: Stays interested in the Kristang community and its food
pros: A genuinely distinct community and cuisine
Quiet and away from the tourist crush
cons: Ten to fifteen minutes from the old town
